_about: Words and figures for /methodology/ that aren't exam results. Exam numbers live in results.json. Source: usuba-checker-scripts/docs/post/draft.md (v0.7) and its data/ folder.

timeline.title: Teach a small model to write plugins
timeline.what: We fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder 7B and 14B on licensed Omarchy plugins. On a static validator the tuned 7B scored 42 of 56, level with GPT-5.6. Run in real Quickshell, it scored 8.
timeline.learned: A file check can call a plugin valid when it does nothing. Only running it tells you.

timeline.title: Build a grader that matches a real laptop
timeline.what: A headless harness boots the real Omarchy shell and loads the plugin. We calibrated it against a Dell Latitude 7430 running Omarchy 4.0.4: from 44 of 58 agreeing cases to 90 of 90, with no false passes.
timeline.learned: A grader you haven't checked against hardware is a guess.

timeline.title: Fine-tunes lose to stock, and a model games the grader
timeline.what: A tuned 27B scored 4 of 49 and looped on 31 answers; the stock 27B scored 6 with none. In a fix loop, grader passes rose from 5 to 13, but only 4 were real.
timeline.learned: Beat your own base model first. And a test you trust has to survive a model trying to fool it.

timeline.title: Pivot: the Checker Scripts come first
timeline.what: We hardened the grader into the Usuba Checker Scripts and wrote down every rule as a public, versioned standard, each with an id, a reason and a fix.
timeline.learned: Don't train anything against a test that can be gamed. The test comes first.

timeline.title: Sweep thousands of plugins on the Dell Latitude
timeline.what: Every plugin we could find, run on real hardware. An audio plugin rerouted the sound and the shell ran out of memory, so we sandboxed the runs and redid 194 jobs.
timeline.learned: The scripts handle "does it load". What's left is "does it work when you click it".

timeline.title: Data, and Usuba run 1
timeline.what: A 4,592-row training set with provenance on every row, and a first LoRA on Qwen3.5 9B. Its first scores were leaky, it flagged 27 of 29 clean plugins, and it named the real bug for 0 of 33 broken ones.
timeline.learned: Read the answers, not just the accuracy. A better prompt on a stock model beat our first trained run.

timeline.title: Usuba run 2
timeline.what: A much smaller, cleaner set: 221 rows mined from plugin git histories and the Dell Latitude runs, scored on three exams against the same stock model.
timeline.learned: It learned the answer format. The judgment is still the Checker Scripts' job.

validatorVsReal.note: October 12, 2026. The validator only reads files; the real run loads each plugin in Quickshell. The real reference plugins passed 51 of 56. Claude Opus's real-run figure is from its larger run; the regular run scored 27.

graderVsReal.caption: The fix loop: what the grader counted vs. what was real, out of 49
graderVsReal.note: Stock Qwen3.6 27B with up to 3 rounds of grader feedback, October 13. Real passes were counted by reading every plugin, at the start and after round 3.

authority.title: The real laptop
authority.body: Omarchy 4.0.4 on a Dell Latitude 7430: load it, click it, screenshot it, read the logs.
authority.power: The final word on whether a plugin works.

authority.title: The Usuba Checker Scripts
authority.body: Plain code with fixed rules. The same answer every run.
authority.power: Decide pass or fail, rule by rule.

authority.title: The Usuba Checker Model
authority.body: Reads the plugin and the scripts' report, explains, suggests a fix.
authority.power: Advises. It can't overrule the two above.

lessons: Beat your own base model before you try to beat anyone else's.
Read the answers, not just the accuracy.
Check the grader against real hardware, then against a model trying to fool it.
Most of the work is data and labels, not GPUs.
